scrutiny.test: T0 purpose: prismis is meant to run on a person's own machines (docs/IDEA.md); a one-line install per component is what lets someone other than the author adopt it.
scrutiny.failureCase: An install that still needs the repo and toolchains.

scrutiny.test: T1 owners: the per-component split and lock-constraint installs are owned by the Makefile (install-tui, install-cli, install-daemon); the formulas mirror them, and Homebrew's tap.rb owns the tap naming that decided the repo layout.
scrutiny.failureCase: A second, different split of the components.

scrutiny.test: T2 same noun: brew's behavior was read in the installed Homebrew 7.0.7 source (std_pip_args --no-binary=:all:, DEFAULT_NETWORK_ACCESS_ALLOWED, tap.rb naming), not from memory.
scrutiny.failureCase: Design built on remembered brew behavior.

scrutiny.test: T3 degrade: daemon installs download wheels and the TUI builds from source; both stated as sacrifices, and Linux stays on make.

T6 assumption checked: every client-only CLI dependency in cli/uv.lock (16 packages) has a pure-Python wheel and an sdist, so brew's source-only pip path can install them; colorama is Windows-only, so the render script must evaluate markers for macOS and leave it out.
scrutiny.failureCase: A compiled CLI dependency brew cannot build.

scrutiny.test: T7 consumers: the formulas consume the tagged tarball's tui/, cli/ and daemon/ and the two locks; nothing in the repo consumes the formulas; the README is the only doc that names the install path.
scrutiny.failureCase: A consumer broken by the move.

scrutiny.test: T9 six months: CLI resources are generated from the lock and a test fails on drift; the daemon formula reads its constraints from the tarball's lock, so neither carries a hand-maintained version list.
scrutiny.failureCase: A resource list that drifts from the lock.

scrutiny.test: T10 reversibility: removing the tap repo or a formula undoes it; the repo change is packaging files, one [build-system] block and README text.
T11 class, every install path for prismis: make (development, Linux, cerebro), the three formulas (macOS); both pin to the locks.

T20 walk: a reader on a Mac runs `brew install nickpending/prismis/prismis-tui nickpending/prismis/prismis-cli`, edits [remote] in config.toml per the caveats, runs `prismis-cli list --limit 1`, then `prismis`; a host owner runs `brew install nickpending/prismis/prismis-daemon`, follows its caveats, and `brew services start prismis-daemon`.
scrutiny.failureCase: A step the caveats do not cover.
